recent_posts.title: Understanding market inefficiencies and fair value gaps in trading
recent_posts.summary: Market inefficiencies occur when price moves rapidly through certain levels, creating 'void areas' where no trading activity took place. These gaps form because traders couldn't enter or exit positions during rapid price movements. Markets tend to fill these fair value gaps over time as price naturally gravitates back to areas with no liquidity, causing it to fall through and reach previous levels.

recent_posts.title: Market Monkey launches as the new Crypto Watch
recent_posts.summary: Market Monkey, formerly Crypto Watch, is a fast and user-friendly trading platform offering features such as customizable charts, orderflow analytics, and real-time market data. Built by a small team, it aims to provide users with the ability to tailor their trading setup and supports multiple exchanges and tickers. Still in beta, it promises future enhancements like aggregated heat maps and custom layouts.

recent_posts.title: How to finish projects effectively
recent_posts.summary: The content emphasizes the importance of mindset over skill in completing projects. The author shares personal experiences of starting from scratch, facing criticism, and persisting despite challenges. Key strategies include involving others to maintain accountability, asking for money to stay motivated, and filtering out distracting influences from social media. The core message is to embrace and push through periods of boredom and demotivation, remaining consistent to achieve success.

recent_posts.title: Golang to Odin: Key Migration Insights
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses the migration from Golang to Odin for building a prop trading terminal called Market Monkey. It highlights the reasons for the switch, including performance improvements and ease of use. The post compares coding paradigms and memory management between the two languages, emphasizing the simplicity and lack of syntactic sugar in Odin. Additionally, it touches on trade-offs such as the absence of a garbage collector in Odin, which requires more manual memory management.

recent_posts.title: Why I switched from Golang to Odin for my desktop app
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses the author's journey in transitioning from Golang to another language for their project's front-end. Despite Golang's strengths in backend development, the author faced performance issues with WebAssembly. They explored various languages like Rust, Zig, and Odin, finally choosing Odin due to its simplicity and suitability for their needs. The author values learning through struggle and is committed to building their application with Odin while continuing to use Golang for the backend.

recent_posts.title: The Actor Model in GO part 2 - Maybe Game Server?
recent_posts.summary: This post continues the series on the actor model in Golang using the Hollywood framework. It covers advanced topics like spawning child actors, the concept of poison pills for stopping actors gracefully, and utilizing event streams to broadcast messages to multiple actors. The post also hints at building a complete game engine using actors in future episodes. Follow along for detailed explanations and code examples.

recent_posts.title: Coding Cryptos Best Trading Terminal - Architectural Problems
How I structured a massive Golang project
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses how Anthony structured his massive Golang project, covering both the server and the front-end. The server uses the Hollywood actor model framework and TimeScaleDB for time series data. The front-end includes a desktop application built with the Ebit game engine for low-level control, and a headless UI with Ebit UI. He emphasizes keeping the folder structure flat to avoid import cycle dependencies and mentions using a single global variable for ease. Common patterns in Golang like handling assets, Docker integration, and managing types and settings are also highlighted.

top_posts.title: Why Go shines for building crypto market analysis tools
top_posts.summary: Market Monkey is a liquidity orderflow and technical analysis platform for crypto markets, built entirely in Go. The platform processes data using an actor engine and supports both client-side and potential server hosting for continuous access. The developer emphasizes the speed, performance, and straightforward syntax of Go, making it an optimal choice for rapid project development despite some criticisms. Future-proofing for WebAssembly was considered, and the developer offers lifetime updates through a one-time purchase with community support via Discord.
